core_idea: People can see themselves as unique individuals or as interchangeable members of a group, depending on context. When a social category becomes salient, people define themselves in group terms (depersonalization) and take on the group's norms, which explains group behaviour, conformity, stereotyping and leadership.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: When and why do people act as group members rather than as individuals?
How do context and comparison make a group identity salient?
Typical data: experiments, surveys, discourse analysis.
common_mistakes: Treating it as the same theory as social identity theory.
Assuming one identity is always active; salience depends on context.
Treating stereotypes only as errors; the theory sees them as context-dependent judgements.
